description: Self-evolving Context Database for AI Agents. Unify Agent Memory, Knowledge RAG and Skills.

sources.entry: openviking - A context database for AI agents that unifies memory, resources, and skills.

summary.one_liner: OpenViking is an open-source context database for AI agents that stores knowledge, memory, and skills in one virtual filesystem under viking:// URIs.
summary.what_it_does: It organizes agent context as a browsable filesystem where agents use commands like ls, tree, read, write, and grep, and users can open directories to inspect and edit what an agent knows. Directories get generated L0 abstracts and L1 overviews so agents can judge relevance before loading full L2 content. Semantic search (find, search) can be scoped to a project or memory subtree rather than a flat vector pool. Committing a session archives the conversation and extracts memories as Markdown files. The project ships an ov CLI, Python, Go and TypeScript SDKs, an HTTP API, and integrations for coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode, plus an optional VikingBot agent framework.
use_cases: give coding agents persistent memory across sessions
index project docs and code for retrieval-augmented generation
inspect and edit what an AI agent remembers
store and reuse agent skills and task experience
scope semantic search to a project directory
self-host a memory backend for agent frameworks
how_to_run: uv tool install openviking --upgrade && openviking-server init
notable: Virtual filesystem (viking:// URIs) for agent memory, resources and skills that can be browsed and edited directly
Tiered context loading: L0 abstract, L1 overview, L2 full content, so agents read summaries before source
Directory-scoped retrieval, with the README citing the TrieHI directory-aware index
Sessions committed as readable Markdown memories
Hosted Volcengine service option and a self-managed commercial edition alongside the open-source server
caveats: Server-side use requires a model provider with an embedding model and a VLM, set up through the init wizard
Desktop app is beta and only for macOS and Windows x64; the memory installer needs macOS or Linux with Node.js 18+
Open-source server is AGPLv3; the README says auth should be configured before exposing it beyond localhost
Hosted service offers only the first 50 files free; plans and limits are in the service documentation
